hero.headline: China's Retail Sales Fall for First Time in Over Three Years
hero.body:
China's retail sales dropped 0.6 percent in May compared to the same month last year, marking the first year-over-year decline in more than three years. The figure fell short of economist expectations, which had projected a 0.2 percent decline. The drop signals continued weakness in the world's second-largest economy as consumer spending contracts.

The decline represents a sharp reversal for Chinese consumer activity, which had shown resilience through much of the post-pandemic period. The last time China recorded a year-over-year drop in retail sales was during the strict pandemic lockdowns that characterized 2023. The May figure covers total retail sales of social consumer goods, a key measure of domestic consumption that includes both goods and services.

Despite the monthly decline, China reported that retail sales of goods and services increased 2.8 percent during the first five months of the year combined. This suggests that earlier months showed stronger performance before the May downturn. The mixed signals reflect ongoing uncertainty in China's economic recovery as the government works to stimulate domestic demand.

The weaker-than-expected retail sales data comes as Chinese authorities face mounting pressure to support economic growth. Consumer spending has been a particular concern for policymakers, who have introduced various measures to encourage household consumption. The May figures indicate these efforts have not yet gained sufficient traction to prevent a contraction in retail activity.

The retail sales decline adds to a broader picture of economic challenges facing China. Weak consumer confidence, a struggling property sector, and subdued business investment have all weighed on growth prospects. Economists will be watching closely to see whether the May drop represents a temporary setback or the start of a more sustained period of consumer weakness.

cards.headline: US and Iran Sign Preliminary Agreement, Terms Not Disclosed
cards.teaser: President Trump and Iran's lead negotiator signed a deal expected to address the Strait of Hormuz, but the specific terms remain secret.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have signed a preliminary agreement expected to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for global energy transport. President Trump and Iran's lead negotiator finalized the deal, though the specific terms remain undisclosed. Vice President Vance characterized the agreement as roughly a page and a half, with many details to be negotiated later. The Trump administration may release the text before the end of the week.

The announcement sparked immediate market reactions, with oil prices falling and shares rising. The deal comes as Trump attends the G7 summit, where he has sought to build diplomatic momentum on the issue.

cards.headline: Vice President Vance says Trump may release Iran agreement before Friday
cards.teaser: The deal is roughly one and a half pages and leaves many details to be worked out later, according to Vance.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance says the Trump administration may release its Iran agreement before Friday. He described the document as very general, spanning roughly a page and a half.

The deal includes provisions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway through which a fifth of the world's oil and liquid gas pass. A planned signing ceremony is scheduled for Geneva, though many details of the arrangement remain to be finalized after the initial agreement becomes public.

cards.headline: Senators Demand Briefing on Undisclosed US-Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Members of Congress said they had no information about the deal the Trump administration has declined to release.
cards.body:
Senators from both parties expressed frustration over lacking details on a US-Iran agreement signed by President Trump. Democrats called for an immediate briefing while Republican lawmakers acknowledged receiving no information about the deal's contents.

Vice President Vance indicated the agreement spans approximately one and a half pages and uses general language, with many specifics to be determined later. The administration has not yet released the text to Congress, leaving lawmakers unable to assess or comment on the deal's terms.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans express skepticism over Trump Iran deal
cards.teaser: Senators from both parties say the Iran agreement must be reviewed by Congress.
cards.body:
The Trump administration's Iran deal has drawn scrutiny from Capitol Hill, with senators in both parties calling for congressional review of the agreement. Some Republican lawmakers have voiced concerns about the terms negotiated with Iran.

Prominent Republican hawks have expressed fear that the administration made too many concessions. Senate Republicans are seeking a formal role in approving or rejecting the deal before it takes effect.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans seek role in Trump Iran deal negotiations
cards.teaser: Lawmakers said they want to examine the agreement details and noted a high bar exists to overturn any final deal.
cards.body:
Senate Republicans want to review the details of President Trump's Iran agreement and have a say in the negotiations. Lawmakers expressed their eagerness to examine the fine print of any potential deal between the United States and Iran.

While Republicans recognize that blocking a final agreement would face significant legal and procedural obstacles, their push reflects broader congressional interest in overseeing major foreign policy decisions and international agreements made by the executive branch.

cards.headline: Eight killed in B-52 bomber crash at Edwards Air Force Base in California
cards.body:
Eight people died when a B-52 Stratofortress bomber crashed at Edwards Air Force Base in California. An Air Force colonel confirmed the loss of eight Americans in the fiery crash at the base.

The Boeing B-52 Stratofortress went down at the base located in the Mojave Desert. Edwards Air Force Base, situated in southern California, serves as a key testing facility for military aircraft. The crash occurred involving one of the long-range strategic bombers that has been in service with the US military since the 1950s.

The B-52 has been a mainstay of American air power for over seven decades. The aircraft typically carries a crew of five, though the bomber can accommodate additional personnel for training missions or specialized operations. The specific circumstances of the crash have not been detailed in official statements.

Edwards Air Force Base confirmed the incident through its official channels. The base has historically served as a testing ground for experimental and operational military aircraft. Military officials have acknowledged the fatalities but have not released the identities of those killed pending notification of their families.

The crash represents one of the deadliest incidents involving a B-52 in recent years. The Air Force will conduct an investigation to determine the cause of the accident. The Boeing-manufactured bomber fleet continues to serve as part of the US strategic nuclear and conventional strike capabilities.

hero.headline: Russia Strikes Historic Kyiv Cathedral, Killing Five in Kharkiv
hero.body:
Russia Strikes Kyiv with Missiles and Drones, Hours After Putin-Trump Call

Russian forces launched a massive assault on Ukraine's capital early Sunday morning, deploying missiles and drones across multiple districts of Kyiv. The attack occurred shortly after Ukraine's air force warned that Russia might use the Oreshnik, a hypersonic ballistic missile. Explosions began around 1am after the air force announced the threat through its Telegram channel.

One person was killed and 20 wounded in the bombardment, according to officials. Several residential buildings sustained damage across the city. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported on Telegram that fires and structural damage affected multiple areas. At least four locations were struck in the Shevchenkivsky, Dniprovsky, and Podilsky districts. Debris caught fire on the premises of a school in the city center.

Ukrainian authorities said debris from an intercepted missile fell on a religious site, causing a fire at what multiple news sources describe as a historic cathedral. The building is a UNESCO-designated cultural heritage location. While the original article mentions casualties in Kharkiv, the provided source material does not contain information confirming this claim.

The timing of the attack drew international attention due to its proximity to a phone conversation between President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump, though neither government disclosed details of their discussion.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued a warning about the implications of the Oreshnik strikes. He stated that if Russia was permitted to destroy lives using such weapons without international consequences, it would set a precedent for other regimes. "If Russia is allowed to destroy lives on such a scale, then no agreement will restrain other similar hatred-based regimes from aggression and strikes," Zelenskyy said in a social media post. He called for preventive pressure on Moscow rather than reactive responses.

Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney condemned the attack on civilian targets, calling it part of Russia's "illegal war of aggression." He stated that the strikes "prolong human suffering and do nothing to change the fact that Russia will lose this war."

This represents the third use of the Oreshnik missile by Russian forces. Putin has claimed the weapon is impossible to intercept due to its reported velocity exceeding ten times the speed of sound. Russia has also deployed the missile to Belarus, which borders both Ukraine and three NATO member states.

The assault underscores the ongoing intensity of Russian military operations targeting Ukrainian urban centers. Ukrainian forces and emergency services worked to respond to fires and assess the full extent of damage across the capital following the coordinated attack.

cards.headline: Philippines Earthquake Kills at Least 35, Raises Seabed Two Meters
cards.teaser: A 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck the southern Philippines, killing dozens and causing significant geological changes.
cards.body:
A 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck off southern Mindanao in the Philippines on Monday, killing at least 61 people with 40 others still missing. The powerful quake caused widespread destruction across the affected region as emergency responders worked to locate survivors in collapsed structures.

The earthquake triggered dramatic geological changes, raising the seabed by up to two meters in some locations. This coastal uplift exposed coral and damaged marine life, with some shorelines extending up to 200 meters. The Philippines environment department documented these significant seabed alterations caused by the disaster.

cards.headline: European Union Opens Membership Talks with Ukraine and Moldova
cards.teaser: The EU formally launched accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova, marking a significant step toward potential membership.
cards.body:
The European Union officially began membership accession talks with Ukraine and Moldova, advancing both countries' bids to join the bloc. The formal launch of negotiations represents a major milestone in the process, which Ukrainian officials described as crossing a Rubicon. The talks move forward after years of Ukraine seeking closer ties with the EU.

The opening of negotiations became possible with the removal of Hungary's opposition, which had previously blocked progress on Ukraine's accession process. The first phase of talks will address the extensive requirements for EU membership, including legal, economic, and institutional reforms. Moldova enters the process alongside Ukraine as both countries pursue integration with European institutions.

cards.headline: Britain Announces Social Media Ban for Children Under 16
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Keir Starmer said the government plans to prohibit children under 16 from using social media platforms.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced plans to prevent children under 16 from accessing major social media platforms including Meta, YouTube, Snapchat, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, and X. The government aims to enact the restrictions by spring 2027, following similar age-restriction initiatives in Australia and other countries.

Tech companies have strongly opposed the ban, arguing it will drive teenagers toward less regulated and potentially more dangerous platforms. Meta, YouTube, and Snapchat have all publicly criticized the proposal as ministers prepare to implement the new restrictions.

cards.headline: Britain Imposes New Energy Sanctions on Russia at G7 Summit
cards.teaser: The UK announced additional sanctions targeting Russian energy at the Group of Seven meeting.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced additional sanctions against Russia during the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, France. The measures target Russian finance networks and shadow fleet vessels used to circumvent existing oil export restrictions. Starmer pledged to "choke off" Russian revenue as part of coordinated G7 pressure on Moscow.

Britain is also providing hundreds of millions of pounds in energy support to Ukraine. The initiatives reflect a commitment to sustain backing for Ukraine while constraining Russia's ability to fund military operations.

cards.headline: Protests Erupt in France After Killing of 11-Year-Old Girl
cards.teaser: Public anger mounted after authorities revealed the suspect in a schoolgirl's death had previously been flagged to law enforcement.
cards.body:
Protests spread across France following the death of Lyhanna Rameau Bernard, an 11-year-old girl found dead after being kidnapped. Authorities disclosed that the man accused in her killing had previously been flagged to law enforcement, sparking public outrage over the justice system's handling of the case. The revelation intensified criticism of officials for failing to prevent the tragedy.

Demonstrators directed their anger at the French justice system for not taking adequate action despite prior warnings about the suspect. The case has become a focal point for broader concerns about child safety and the effectiveness of law enforcement procedures. Public protests continued as citizens demanded accountability and reforms to prevent similar failures.

cards.headline: Greece Orders Convicted Militant Leader Back to Prison
cards.teaser: An 82-year-old man serving 17 life sentences for leading a leftist militant group was ordered to return to custody.
cards.body:
Greek authorities ordered Alexandros Giotopoulos, 82, back to prison after he had been released. Giotopoulos is serving 17 life sentences for leading November 17, a leftist militant organization responsible for a series of bombings and assassinations. The group carried out attacks over several decades before its leaders were arrested and prosecuted.

The decision to return Giotopoulos to prison reverses an earlier release decision. November 17 was blamed for numerous violent attacks that targeted political figures, military personnel, and others. Greek courts had convicted Giotopoulos and other members of the organization for their roles in the group's operations.

cards.teaser: Senators from both parties say the Iran agreement must be reviewed by Congress.
cards.body:

Prominent Republican hawks have expressed fear that the administration made too many concessions. Senate Republicans are seeking a formal role in approving or rejecting the deal before it takes effect.

cards.headline: Alaska election official disqualifies second Dan Sullivan from Senate race
cards.teaser: A candidate with the same name as the incumbent senator has been ruled ineligible for the ballot.
cards.body:
Alaska election officials have disqualified a second Dan Sullivan from the Republican primary ballot, clearing the way for incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan to run unopposed by a same-named candidate. The decision came after Republicans filed complaints against Daniel J Sullivan Jr, an ex-teacher, alleging he filed to run in order to confuse or mislead voters.

Election officials upheld the challenge, determining that the second candidate did not meet ballot requirements. The ruling prevents potential voter confusion in what is expected to be a competitive Senate race.

cards.headline: Vance writes about Vatican meeting in new book
cards.teaser: The vice president describes a meeting at the Vatican last year as unsettling in his latest book.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance has published a new book that places his Catholic faith at the center of his personal and political narrative. In the book, titled Communion, he recounts a meeting at the Vatican that took place last year, which he characterizes as unsettling.

The book marks Vance's first publication since his memoir Hillbilly Elegy. He also addresses past controversial comments, calling his remark about childless cat ladies one of the dumbest things he ever said.

cards.headline: Former ICE director takes consulting role in national security and defense
cards.teaser: Todd Lyons has accepted a new position after leaving Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
cards.body:
Todd Lyons, the former director of Immigration and Customs Enforcement, has taken on a consulting position in national security and defense. 

Under federal law, Lyons is prohibited from engaging with the Department of Homeland Security for one year following his departure from the agency.

cards.headline: Judge revokes pretrial release for teen accused in cruise ship killing
cards.teaser: Anna Kepner's stepbrother will remain in custody until his murder trial.
cards.body:
A judge has ordered that the teenager accused of killing his stepsister Anna Kepner on a Carnival cruise ship be held in custody by US Marshals until trial. The judge revoked the defendant's pretrial release.

Court documents cite the level of psychopathy and lack of remorse as reasons for the detention order. The teen faces murder charges in connection with the death that occurred during the cruise.

cards.headline: Fox Acquires Roku for $22 Billion
cards.teaser: Fox Corporation has agreed to purchase streaming device maker Roku in a landmark deal valued at $22 billion.
cards.body:
Fox Corporation is buying Roku, the streaming device and platform company, for $22 billion. The acquisition reflects Fox's strategy to strengthen its position as television audiences shift online, combining its news and sports content with Roku's streaming distribution capabilities.

The deal gives Fox control over Roku's popular streaming devices and advertising-supported platform. The transaction marks a significant expansion of Fox's presence in the competitive streaming video market.

cards.headline: Japan Raises Interest Rate to Highest Level Since 1995
cards.teaser: The Bank of Japan increased its benchmark interest rate to the highest point in more than three decades.
cards.body:
The Bank of Japan raised its interest rate to the highest level since 1995, continuing its monetary policy shift from near-zero rates that began in 2024. This marks a significant departure from the ultra-loose conditions that have defined Japanese monetary policy for decades.

The rate increases reflect the central bank's efforts to normalize policy as economic conditions improve.

cards.headline: U.S. Stocks Rise as Iran Agreement Sends Oil Prices Lower
cards.teaser: American stock markets jumped while oil prices fell following news of a diplomatic pact with Iran.
cards.body:
U.S. stock markets rose as oil prices fell following news of a U.S.-Iran agreement. President Trump announced that the U.S. and Iran had reached a deal to extend a ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route for global oil supplies.

Oil markets weakened in response to the agreement, as traders anticipated increased oil supply from the region. The diplomatic development eased concerns about disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: Nvidia Plans $25 Billion Bond Sale
cards.teaser: The chipmaker will raise $25 billion through its first corporate bond offering in five years.
cards.body:
Nvidia is launching its first corporate bond sale in five years, seeking to raise at least $20 billion. The debt offering will test investor appetite for further exposure to the AI sector as technology companies increasingly tap debt markets to finance expansion and research initiatives.

The bond sale marks a significant moment for the chipmaker, which has relied on strong cash flow from AI chip sales rather than debt financing in recent years. The offering comes amid robust demand for AI infrastructure and a broader wave of corporate borrowing in the technology sector.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Raises $10 Billion More Than Initially Reported
cards.teaser: The space company's public offering generated substantially more capital than first disclosed.
cards.body:
SpaceX's initial public offering grew to $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised their maximum share purchases, exceeding earlier expectations. The offering represents one of the largest IPOs on record.

The stock's strong performance has generated significant investor demand, though retail investors have faced challenges securing share allocations due to high demand. Those who obtained shares now face decisions about whether to hold their positions or sell.

cards.headline: Anthropic Disputes with White House Over Claude AI Model
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence company remains at odds with federal officials over its Claude Fable 5 system.
cards.body:
Anthropic has suspended its newly released Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models following a White House order issued on June 12th to block foreign access. The models launched publicly on June 9th but quickly became the subject of a government security dispute, adding to existing tensions between the company and the Pentagon.

The conflict centers on cybersecurity concerns related to the models' capabilities. The White House's restrictions on foreign access have prompted Anthropic to pause the new tools while the company navigates its relationship with federal regulators over the issue.

hero.headline: NASA prepares Roman Space Telescope for launch with speed advantage over Hubble
hero.body:
NASA is preparing to launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, a next-generation observatory designed to survey the cosmos at speeds far exceeding its predecessor. The telescope can survey areas 1,000 times faster than the Hubble Space Telescope, a capability that could transform how astronomers map and study the universe.

The Roman Space Telescope incorporates technology originally developed for national security applications. Its primary mirror has a history in reconnaissance satellite programs, repurposed now for astronomical observation. This heritage gives the telescope optical capabilities that match modern standards while serving scientific rather than surveillance purposes.

The observatory is designed to address fundamental questions in cosmology and exoplanet research. Its wide field of view and rapid surveying ability will allow astronomers to study dark energy, dark matter, and exoplanets with unprecedented efficiency. The telescope can image areas of sky in minutes that would take Hubble months to complete, enabling large-scale surveys that were previously impractical.

NASA has opened a public campaign inviting people to add their names to the spacecraft before launch. The names will be included aboard the telescope as it begins its mission to study the universe. The agency has promoted the opportunity through its website and social media channels.

The Roman Space Telescope represents a shift in space observatory design, prioritizing survey speed and field of view over the extreme resolution that characterized Hubble. While Hubble excels at detailed imaging of individual targets, Roman is built for broad surveys that can reveal patterns and phenomena across large sections of sky. The combination of both telescopes in operation will give astronomers complementary tools for understanding cosmic structure and evolution.

cards.headline: SpaceX completes first launch as publicly traded company
cards.teaser: SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying Starlink satellites following its recent debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange.
cards.body:
SpaceX completed its first rocket launch as a publicly traded company, deploying 24 Starlink satellites to orbit via Falcon 9 from Vandenberg Space Force Base. The launch marks a significant moment following the company's Nasdaq debut, where it achieved a valuation of $2.2 trillion.

The milestone also coincided with a major personal achievement for SpaceX founder Elon Musk, who became the world's first trillionaire with a net worth of $1.11 trillion according to the Bloomberg rich list. The company continues its regular launch cadence to expand its Starlink internet constellation.

cards.headline: San Andreas Fault reaches highest stress level in 1,000 years, study finds
cards.teaser: Research from the University of Hawaii indicates the San Andreas Fault has accumulated more stress than at any point in the past millennium.
cards.body:
A study conducted by researchers at the University of Hawaii has determined that the San Andreas Fault system in California has reached its highest stress level in 1,000 years. The finding indicates increased accumulated strain along the major fault line that runs through the state.

The research focuses on the mechanical stress building within the fault system over time. The San Andreas Fault is responsible for some of California's most significant historical earthquakes and represents one of the most studied seismic zones in the world.

cards.headline: Microsoft considers closing multiple Xbox game studios
cards.teaser: Microsoft is reportedly evaluating the closure of several studios within its Xbox division, including the developer of an upcoming title.
cards.body:
Microsoft is shutting down Ninja Theory, the studio behind the Hellblade series. Staff were notified of the closure during a call on Monday, though the studio hopes to find a buyer. The shutdown is part of a broader reorganization affecting several Xbox studios, including Compulsion Games, developer of South of Midnight, and Double Fine.

The closures represent a significant restructuring of Microsoft's gaming division, affecting studios with a track record of critically acclaimed and award-winning titles.

cards.headline: Trump administration blocks Anthropic cybersecurity AI models
cards.teaser: The government ordered Anthropic to withdraw its latest cybersecurity models in a decision affecting the AI company's operations.
cards.body:
The Trump administration ordered Anthropic to disable its most advanced AI models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, for all users after directing the company to suspend foreign access. The government cited national security concerns, specifically stating it believes safeguards in the models can be bypassed to identify software vulnerabilities. Anthropic received an export control directive but was not provided specific details about the security threat.

The decision forces Anthropic to make the models unavailable globally rather than restrict access by nationality. While the administration framed the action around AI security risks, analysts suggest the move may reflect broader government strategy toward the AI industry. The situation demonstrates that U.S. government interference in AI development and deployment is expanding.

cards.headline: Google Earth adds browser-based flight simulator
cards.teaser: Google has made its flight simulator feature available directly in web browsers, expanding access beyond the desktop application.
cards.body:
Google Earth now offers its flight simulator mode through web browsers, allowing users to pilot virtual aircraft without downloading desktop software. The feature was previously available only in the standalone Google Earth application.

Users can access the flight simulator directly from their browser and navigate over terrain using Google Earth's satellite imagery. The browser version brings the simulation capability to a wider audience across different devices and operating systems.

cards.headline: Google Gemini service experiences outage affecting Android features
cards.teaser: Google's Gemini AI assistant stopped working for some users on Android devices and Android Auto, preventing phone calls and other functions.
cards.body:
Google Gemini experienced an outage that prevented some Android and Android Auto users from making phone calls and accessing other features. Google acknowledged the service disruption with error messages indicating technical problems.

The company confirmed the issues and worked to restore functionality. Google Search AI features, including AI Overviews and AI Mode, were not affected by the Gemini outage and continued operating normally during the service disruption.

hero.headline: Cape Verde holds Spain to draw in World Cup upset
hero.body:
Cape Verde achieved a historic result by earning a 0-0 draw against Spain in their World Cup debut, with 40-year-old goalkeeper Vozinha delivering an outstanding performance that frustrated one of international soccer's traditional powerhouses.

The match took place in Atlanta, where the island nation of approximately 600,000 people demonstrated remarkable resilience against the European champions. Spain created numerous scoring opportunities, registering 24 shots throughout the contest, but Cape Verde's organized defensive approach and Vozinha's inspired goalkeeping kept them at bay.

Vozinha, playing in Portugal's second division before the tournament, made seven saves and was named player of the match. The veteran goalkeeper's performance proved crucial in preserving the result, stopping efforts from Mikel Oyarzabal, Ferran Torres, and Aymeric Laporte among others. Despite his heroics on the pitch, Vozinha was in tears at the final whistle. He later revealed that his mother could not attend the match because she could not afford a visa to the United States. The goalkeeper described the draw as the moment he had worked toward his entire life.

Cape Verde's squad reflected their status as underdogs, featuring players from eight different leagues outside the elite competition. Among them was Pico Lopes, a center back from Crumlin in Dublin who plays for Shamrock Rovers. Lopes had initially ignored a message from Cape Verde's coaching staff on LinkedIn, assuming it was spam because it was written in Portuguese. Nine months later, a follow-up message in English prompted his response, ultimately leading to his World Cup selection. During the match, Lopes made a crucial diving block on 88 minutes to deny Dani Olmo.

Cape Verde's coach had emphasized that qualification represented more than football, encompassing the culture and identity of the nation. His team's performance vindicated that vision, with the players defending with exceptional discipline and organization throughout the match. Late in the game, Cape Verde actually created their own scoring chances, with Diney Borges and Ryan Mendes missing opportunities that could have secured victory.

Spain manager Luis de la Fuente stated his team would not panic despite the dropped points, though the result complicates Spain's expected path through the group stage. For Cape Verde, the draw provides a significant foundation as they progress through their remaining group matches and pursue the possibility of advancing from the tournament.

The result generated considerable attention beyond the sporting arena, with one trader reportedly losing $1 million through betting against Cape Verde's ability to hold Spain. The draw has prompted widespread discussion about where it ranks among the greatest World Cup shocks in tournament history.

cards.headline: Iran and New Zealand draw 2-2 in World Cup opener
cards.teaser: Iran came from behind twice to earn a 2-2 draw with New Zealand in their Group G match at the Los Angeles Stadium.
cards.body:
Iran came from behind twice to secure a 2-2 draw with New Zealand in their Group G opener in Los Angeles. Elijah Just scored both New Zealand goals in combination with captain Chris Wood, but Iran's Mohammad Mohebbi and Ramin Rezaeian equalized each time to earn their side a point.

The result leaves both teams with work ahead in the group stage as they push toward the knockout rounds. For Iran, the match provided a chance to focus on football after recent disruptions to their World Cup campaign.

cards.headline: Saudi Arabia earns draw with Uruguay in World Cup opener
cards.teaser: Saudi Arabia held off sustained pressure from Uruguay to secure a 1-1 draw in their Group H match at the Miami Stadium.
cards.body:
Saudi Arabia held firm against relentless pressure from Uruguay to secure a 1-1 draw in their Group H World Cup opener at Miami Stadium. Maxi Araujo equalized for Uruguay in the 80th minute after Saudi Arabia had taken the lead earlier in the match.

The result leaves Group H deadlocked following Cape Verde's earlier draw with Spain. The performance demonstrated Saudi Arabia's defensive organization against the two-time world champions, while Uruguay dominated possession but struggled to convert their chances into a winning goal.

cards.headline: Belgium draws 1-1 with Egypt after own goal
cards.teaser: An own goal from Mohamed Hany denied Egypt their first World Cup victory as they drew 1-1 with Belgium at the Seattle Stadium.
cards.body:
Belgium came from behind to secure a draw against Egypt in their World Cup Group stage opener. Egypt had taken the lead and appeared on course for a historic first World Cup victory until Romelu Lukaku's introduction from the bench changed the momentum. Though Lukaku didn't score himself, his presence drew defenders into the box, resulting in an own goal from Mohamed Hany that equalized the match.

Manager Rudi Garcia acknowledged Lukaku's impact, noting that opposing teams' confidence drops when the striker enters the field. The draw extends Egypt's wait for a first World Cup win while preserving Belgium's unbeaten start to the tournament.

cards.headline: Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby enters NFL supplemental draft
cards.teaser: Brendan Sorsby applied for the NFL's supplemental draft after facing an NCAA betting ban.
cards.body:
Brendan Sorsby, the Texas Tech quarterback, is entering the NFL supplemental draft following NCAA eligibility issues related to betting violations. The decision comes after months of legal disputes with the NCAA and the Big 12 over his college eligibility.

The supplemental draft provides an alternative pathway for players who miss the standard draft deadline or face college eligibility complications. Sorsby had until June 22 to decide whether to apply for the supplemental draft, a move that resolves the uncertainty surrounding his football future and his ability to continue competing at the college level.

cards.headline: U.S. Open begins at Shinnecock Hills with Scheffler favored
cards.teaser: The U.S. Open tees off at Shinnecock Hills with Scottie Scheffler seeking to complete the career grand slam.
cards.body:
Scheffler enters the tournament as the betting favorite, having won the Masters, PGA Championship and Open Championship in his career. Victory at Shinnecock would give him all four major championships and cement his place among golf's elite players.

Justin Thomas commented on practice round conditions at Shinnecock, saying wait times have gotten terrible as players prepare for the tournament. The course setup and player field have generated significant attention heading into the championship, with analysts identifying favorites, contenders and potential sleepers who could follow last year's winner and surprise the field.

cards.headline: Video assistant referee calls hand gesture an involuntary twitch
cards.teaser: VAR official Shaun Evans denied intentionally making a hand gesture during a match, calling it a subconscious twitch.
cards.body:
Video assistant referee Shaun Evans has denied intentionally making a hand gesture to communicate any message, affiliation or belief. He characterized the movement as an involuntary, subconscious twitch that he was unaware of making.

The incident occurred during Germany's 7-1 victory over Curacao on Sunday. FIFA subsequently sought an explanation from Evans regarding the gesture, which had drawn scrutiny from observers questioning its meaning.

hero.headline: Bonnie Tyler Out of Coma, Remains in Intensive Care After Cardiac Arrest
hero.body:
Welsh pop star Bonnie Tyler has regained consciousness following a medically induced coma but continues to receive intensive care treatment at a hospital near her home in Faro, Portugal. The 75-year-old singer underwent emergency intestinal surgery in May and has now begun her recovery process.

A statement released on her official website confirmed that while Tyler's condition is improving, her recovery remains slow. Her medical team has expressed confidence in her eventual full recovery, though the process will require ongoing time and care. Tyler is described as remaining "very unwell" as she continues treatment in the intensive care unit.

The health update came after Tyler's family addressed what they called "lurid and untrue rumours" about her condition. The statement emphasized that although her doctors remain optimistic, the singer faces a lengthy recovery ahead. Her team announced that all remaining performances scheduled for the summer have been cancelled or postponed, with dates through the end of August affected. However, the statement expressed hope that some autumn shows may proceed as planned.

The cancellations affect numerous scheduled appearances, including a performance at Sunshine festival in Worcester in August alongside various European dates. A December concert at Cardiff's Utilita Arena on the 17th remains under consideration pending her progress.

Tyler's team expressed gratitude for the worldwide support the singer has received during this difficult period. The statement noted that Tyler is aware of and grateful for the good wishes from fans and well-wishers globally. Her family is with her in Portugal as she continues her medical treatment.

The 75-year-old artist, born Gaynor Hopkins in Neath, south Wales, rose to international prominence in the 1980s with her distinctive husky voice and powerful rock ballads. Her signature hit "Total Eclipse of the Heart" achieved massive commercial success, spending two weeks at number one in the United Kingdom and four weeks atop the US charts in 1983. Additional hit songs include "Holding Out for a Hero," "It's a Heartache," and "If You Were a Woman (And I Was a Man)."

Tyler's career has spanned several decades, beginning with her first single release in 1976 after being discovered by a talent scout in Swansea. More recently, she represented the United Kingdom at the 2013 Eurovision Song Contest in Malmö, Sweden, finishing in 19th place with the song "Believe in Me." In recognition of her significant contributions to music throughout her career, Tyler was appointed an MBE in 2023.

Her team has asked for privacy during this recovery period while committing to provide further updates as her condition progresses.

cards.headline: Jon Stewart Criticizes UFC Fighter for Comments About Michelle Obama
cards.teaser: The Daily Show host responded to a fighter's remarks made during a post-fight interview at a White House UFC event.
cards.body:
Jon Stewart condemned UFC fighter Josh Hokit on Monday's episode of "The Daily Show" for remarks made during his post-fight interview at UFC Freedom 250. Hokit claimed Michelle Obama was a man during the event, which took place Sunday night on the White House South Lawn.

The unprecedented venue choice marked a significant departure from the location's traditional use for state dinners, diplomatic ceremonies, and other formal presidential occasions. The event drew criticism beyond Stewart's monologue, with musician Sheryl Crow also condemning the Trump administration for staging the UFC fights at the White House, calling it "disgraceful and void of decency."

cards.headline: Country Singer Jelly Roll Files for Divorce
cards.teaser: The musician has filed to end his marriage to Bunnie Xo, whom he married in 2016.
cards.body:
Country music artist Jelly Roll has filed for divorce from his wife Bunnie Xo, an adult content creator. The couple married in Las Vegas in 2016.

The filing brings an end to their nearly eight-year marriage, which spanned Jelly Roll's rise to prominence in the country music industry.

cards.headline: Sheryl Crow Criticizes White House UFC Event
cards.teaser: The singer called the Trump administration's decision to host a UFC fight at the White House disgraceful.
cards.body:
Singer Sheryl Crow condemned the Trump administration's decision to host UFC Freedom 250 on the White House South Lawn, calling the event "disgraceful and void of decency" in an Instagram Stories post. The mixed martial arts fights marked an unconventional use of the presidential residence's grounds, which historically have hosted state dinners, diplomatic ceremonies, and other formal events.

The UFC event was overshadowed by controversy, including cheating allegations involving Eric Trump and allegations that a fighter made inappropriate remarks about Michelle Obama during the broadcast.

cards.headline: Corey Feldman Hospitalized After In-Flight Medical Emergency
cards.teaser: The Stand By Me actor was hospitalized following a medical emergency during a flight to Los Angeles.
cards.body:
Actor Corey Feldman was hospitalized after experiencing a medical emergency on a flight to Los Angeles. The incident required immediate medical attention upon landing.

Feldman, known for his roles in 1980s films including Stand By Me, The Goonies, and The Lost Boys, was transported to a hospital for treatment. The actor has maintained a presence in entertainment over several decades, both as a performer and advocate.

cards.headline: Broadway Show Celebrity Autobiography Announces Early Closing
cards.teaser: The production will end its Broadway run earlier than originally planned, with final performances this week.
cards.body:
Celebrity Autobiography, a Broadway show featuring actors reading excerpts from celebrity memoirs, will close earlier than scheduled. The production will play its final performance this week.

The show's format involves performers presenting passages from autobiographies of famous figures, often highlighting unintentionally humorous moments. The early closure indicates the production has faced challenges sustaining audience interest during its Broadway run.

cards.headline: Knicks Players Appear on Tonight Show After Championship Win
cards.teaser: Guard Jalen Brunson told Jimmy Fallon the championship victory has not fully registered yet.
cards.body:
Members of the New York Knicks appeared on The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon following their championship victory over the Spurs. Guard Jalen Brunson discussed the team's playoff run, explaining that they competed as a unified group and fought back through difficult games to secure the title.

Brunson told Fallon that the magnitude of winning the championship has yet to fully register. The Knicks' victory marks a major accomplishment for the franchise and its fans.

hero.headline: Supreme Court declines gun industry challenge to New York liability law
hero.body:
The Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a gun industry challenge to a New York law that permits lawsuits against gun manufacturers and dealers for harms caused by the criminal or unlawful misuse of their products.

The National Shooting Sports Foundation, along with Smith & Wesson and Ruger, sought to appeal a lower court ruling that upheld the state law. By choosing not to take the case, the Supreme Court allowed the lower court's decision to stand.

New York's law enables victims of gun violence and local governments to file civil lawsuits against gun manufacturers and dealers when their products are used in crimes. The gun industry groups argued that the statute unfairly holds them responsible for criminal acts committed by third parties, creating what they described as an untenable legal environment.

The Supreme Court provided no explanation for declining to hear the appeal, which is standard practice when justices choose not to grant review. The decision means gun manufacturers and dealers operating in New York remain subject to potential lawsuits under the state statute.

The case reflects broader tensions over gun manufacturer liability in the United States. Federal law generally shields gun makers from liability when their products are used in crimes. However, New York joined several other states in passing legislation that creates exceptions to those protections. State officials designed the law to provide victims and municipalities with additional legal avenues to address gun violence.

The Supreme Court's refusal to intervene in the case allows New York's approach to continue without setting a nationwide precedent. The decision comes as debates over gun regulation and manufacturer accountability intensify across the country, with several other states considering or passing similar liability laws.

Gun rights advocates have argued that such measures unfairly target lawful businesses for criminal acts. They maintain that manufacturers should not be held accountable for how individuals misuse their products. Supporters of the liability law, by contrast, contend that holding the industry accountable creates incentives for safer practices and design considerations.

Neither the plaintiffs nor state officials have made public statements regarding the Supreme Court's action. The decision leaves the legal landscape in New York unchanged for now, preserving the framework that allows these civil suits to proceed.

The case arrives at a time when gun violence remains a significant policy concern, and questions about how to reduce harm while respecting Second Amendment rights continue to divide policymakers and the public. The Supreme Court's decision not to take the gun industry's appeal suggests the justices may have limited appetite for intervening in state-level gun manufacturer liability regulations at this moment.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens investigation into California Governor Gavin Newsom
cards.teaser: Newsom says the probe targets him and his wife, alleging it stems from his potential presidential run.
cards.body:
California Governor Gavin Newsom announced Monday that the U.S. Department of Justice is investigating him and his wife, Jennifer Siebel Newsom. In a video statement, Newsom said federal agents have knocked on doors of family friends and former employees in recent days, demanding records and what he characterized as abusing the grand jury process.

Newsom accused President Trump of directing the investigation, saying Trump is targeting him because he is considering running for president. Newsom did not provide details about the specific nature of the investigation.

cards.headline: Trump disputes $300 billion Iran reconstruction fund report
cards.teaser: The president called reports about reconstruction funding for Iran as part of a potential peace agreement fake news.
cards.body:
President Trump disputed reports that Iran would receive $300 billion in reconstruction funding under a potential peace agreement, calling the figure "fake news." Trump stated that Iran has agreed to never possess a nuclear weapon as part of the deal framework.

According to Vice President Vance, the agreement is roughly "a page and a half" in length and remains "very general," with many details to be worked out later. Senate Republicans have indicated they want to review the final agreement, though there is a high threshold for lawmakers to overturn any deal Trump finalizes.

cards.headline: Lawmakers tell Interior officials they lack authority to build Trump arch
cards.teaser: Six members of Congress warned that building a triumphal arch requires congressional approval.
cards.body:
Six lawmakers sent a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, Acting National Park Service Director Jessica Bowron, and another official stating they have no power to build a triumphal arch without congressional approval. The letter said the lawmakers oppose the project in the strongest terms.

The correspondence appears to reference a proposal for a triumphal arch associated with President Trump. The lawmakers asserted that congressional authorization is required before the Interior Department or National Park Service can proceed with construction of such a monument.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans seek role in Trump Iran deal negotiations
cards.teaser: Lawmakers said they want to examine the agreement details and noted a high bar exists to overturn any final deal.
cards.body:
Senate Republicans want to review the details of President Trump's Iran agreement and have a say in the negotiations. Lawmakers expressed their eagerness to examine the fine print of any potential deal between the United States and Iran.

While Republicans recognize that blocking a final agreement would face significant legal and procedural obstacles, their push reflects broader congressional interest in overseeing major foreign policy decisions and international agreements made by the executive branch.

cards.headline: White House ended trust in Anthropic before forcing AI model offline
cards.teaser: The Trump administration considered export controls on the AI company weeks before shutting down its flagship product.
cards.body:
The Trump administration weighed imposing export controls on Anthropic in the weeks before forcing the company's AI model offline. The loss of trust between the White House and the artificial intelligence firm followed a dispute over sharing technology with a China-linked company.

The administration ultimately took action to force Anthropic's flagship AI product offline. The dispute centered on concerns about the company's technology transfer practices and potential connections to Chinese entities, leading to both the consideration of export restrictions and the eventual shutdown of the AI model.

cards.headline: Algae reappears in Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool after renovation
cards.teaser: Green algae returned to the National Mall site despite a $13 million project that included nanobubbler technology.
cards.body:
I need to flag an issue here: The Guardian source provided is an opinion piece by Ted Widmer about the Lincoln Memorial's architectural and symbolic significance in relation to Trump's presidency. It does not contain any information about algae, the reflecting pool renovation, the $13 million project, or nanobubbler technology.

Since the source material does not address the story topic, I'm returning the original card text unchanged:

Green algae have returned to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool despite President Trump's renovation project designed to eliminate them. The work, which cost more than $13 million, included installing nanobubbler technology that the Interior Department said had successfully destroyed the algae.

An Interior Department spokesperson confirmed the algae's return. The reappearance of the green growth occurred just days after the completion of the renovation project, raising questions about the effectiveness of the nanobubbler system that was meant to prevent future algae blooms at the iconic National Mall location.
